headline: High: aci’s broad egress and CRM/email access can leak or act on Prefect workflow data; shared MCP/function-call pathways also create prompt-injection and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can use direct function calls or an MCP server and ingests email/Slack/Notion/Sheets content; Prefect orchestrates workflows and can consume upstream outputs. A shared MCP or file bridge would let attacker-controlled content from aci influence Prefect instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF aci output is copied into a Prefect task payload or workflow parameter without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared MCP server or shared workspace, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable free-form text handoff between agents.
Add a strict schema validator for any aci-to-Prefect payload.
Require allowlisted commands only in MCP/tool calls.
Insert a human review step before Prefect executes aci-derived instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress; Prefect is an orchestrator that can move workflow metadata and call external APIs. If aci forwards sensitive records into Prefect workflows, the pair can exfiltrate sensitive business data to third parties by default. The exact shared workspace is undocumented, so uncertainty does not reduce the blast radius.
conditions: IF aci passes CRM/email/calendar content into Prefect task inputs, those contents may leave the original system boundary.
IF Prefect tasks log or transmit aci-derived payloads to external services, sensitive data can be exposed.
mitigations: Redact PII before any aci-to-Prefect transfer.
Turn off verbose task logging for Prefect runs.
Route sensitive fields through a local-only staging step.
Restrict aci outputs to workflow metadata only.
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on all inter-agent payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad egress, while Prefect is an orchestration system that can coordinate mutable workflows. If both are pointed at the same mutable resources or shared repo/workspace, concurrent writes can conflict. The profiles do not prove a shared directory or lock manager, so this is a plausible but not guaranteed medium risk.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workflow state, repo, or database without locking, updates can race.
IF Prefect and aci share OAuth-backed mutable resources, last-write-wins conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate write targets per agent.
Enable optimistic concurrency or locking on shared resources.
Schedule non-overlapping execution windows.
Use a single writer for each mutable system.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and Prefect is an automation/orchestration layer, so aci output can become Prefect input and then trigger downstream actions. If Prefect treats aci-produced facts as authoritative, a single bad inference can cascade into incorrect workflow execution or external side effects. This interaction is plausible from the profiles alone, so the safer high severity is warranted.
conditions: IF Prefect uses aci output as a task parameter or decision input without verification, errors can propagate.
IF Prefect triggers external actions from aci-derived facts, a mistaken fact can cause downstream harm.
mitigations: Require a verification step before Prefect acts on aci output.
Add confidence thresholds for aci-derived decisions.
Log and diff aci inputs versus Prefect actions.
Limit aci output to suggestions, not commands.
requires-engineering: implement provenance tracking across the workflow.

E_compliance.rationale: aci touches email, CRM, calendar, support, and research data, while Prefect handles workflow metadata and can call external APIs. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated or customer data is routed into Prefect logs, retention, or third-party services. The profiles do not show specific residency or certification gaps, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is included in Prefect workflow metadata or logs, retention obligations may be violated.
IF aci data crosses into a region or service with stricter residency rules, compliance controls may fail.
mitigations: Classify data before passing it to Prefect.
Mask regulated fields in workflow metadata.
Set short retention on Prefect logs.
Review vendor residency and DPA terms before enabling sensitive flows.
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based routing by data class.
